claim_reviews.conclusion: “Employee handbook” matches a book explaining workplace rules and procedures.
claim_reviews.subject: English cue and sense

claim_reviews.conclusion: Valid Indonesian wording for an employee handbook; “pedoman” means guide/manual and “karyawan” means employee.
claim_reviews.subject: Indonesian answer: buku pedoman karyawan

claim_reviews.conclusion: Established Malaysian Malay wording for an employee handbook; exact phrase usage is documented in Malaysian workplace materials.
claim_reviews.subject: Malaysian answer: buku panduan pekerja

claim_reviews.conclusion: “different-common-word” is appropriate: pedoman/panduan and karyawan/pekerja are common regional lexical choices. This is a useful contrast, not a false-friend pair; the forms are semantically aligned.
claim_reviews.evidence_limitation: No dedicated comparative Indonesian–Malaysian lexicographic source was consulted.

response.rationale: Both forms accurately express “employee handbook” and the stated workplace-rules-and-procedures sense. The Indonesian and Malaysian entries use regionally preferred vocabulary; the contrast is useful, though not a strict false-friend distinction.
